outline.h2: How does the UX design San Diego companies need change by sector?
outline.answerHint: The UX design San Diego companies need changes with the sector. Software and SaaS teams need activation and dashboards, life sciences teams need dense data screens with regulatory review, and cybersecurity teams need alert views analysts trust.
points: Card 'Software and SaaS': San Diego Regional EDC counts 28,617 software jobs and 2,949 establishments; one in six innovation economy jobs is in software development. Design focus: onboarding, activation, admin and billing.

Card 'Life sciences software': Biocom counts 61,866 San Diego life sciences jobs at the end of 2025 (down 2.55%). Design focus: lab and clinical data tables, audit trails; HIPAA for patient data, FDA SaMD rules when software has a medical purpose; the client's regulatory team decides which apply.
Card 'Cybersecurity': EDC + Cyber Center of Excellence 2025 study: 14,875 jobs, 1,350 establishments, $4.3 billion impact. Design focus: alert triage, role-based admin, SOC 2 evidence screens.
Card 'AI and wireless': Shield AI and Qualcomm are headquartered in San Diego (only if the fact-checker verifies). Design focus: AI output people check and correct.
Card 'Research spinouts': UC San Diego won nearly $1.8 billion in research awards in FY2026; EvoNexus runs a free incubator. Design focus: turning a lab prototype into a first product (MVP).
Each card body 30–50 words, one number, one design implication. Never say we worked for these companies.

outline.h2: Is a remote UX design company San Diego startups hire a safe choice?
outline.answerHint: Yes, for most AI and SaaS products: research, reviews and user tests all run well online. A local studio fits better when the work needs weekly in-person observation, such as watching scientists use instruments in a wet lab.

faqSection.h2: Questions San Diego founders ask before a UX project
faqSection.answer: Short answers on location, hours, regulated data, start dates, testing and development.

faqs.q: Do you have an office or designers in San Diego?
faqs.a: No. Our only office is in Reston, VA, and our team works remotely with US companies. San Diego teams meet us on video calls inside the shared 9 a.m.–2 p.m. PT window.

faqs.q: Can you design life sciences or health software that handles patient data?
faqs.a: Yes, at the design level: role-based screens, audit trails, consent and data-entry flows. Your regulatory and legal team decides whether HIPAA or FDA Software as a Medical Device rules apply; we design to the requirements they set.

faqs.q: How soon can a San Diego startup start a project?
faqs.a: A senior team usually starts within 1 to 2 weeks of a signed proposal, and dedicated designers start in 1 to 2 weeks. A senior designer replies to every enquiry within one business day, ET.

faqs.q: Do you test designs with real users?
faqs.a: Yes. Risky flows are tested with 5 to 8 target users as clickable prototypes, in remote sessions, so testers can sit anywhere in the US.

faqs.q: Can you also build the product?
faqs.a: Yes. ui-ux.agency is the design team of tkxel, a software engineering company, so you can hire us for design only or for design and development together.

faqs.q: Which accessibility standard do your designs follow?
faqs.a: WCAG 2.2 AA, the W3C standard published as a Recommendation on October 5, 2023, which US teams use to meet ADA and Section 508 expectations.
